subject: Secure SDLC evidence request — supply-chain, CI gates, credential detector artifacts
messages:
From: Acme Security <audit@acme-sec.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Secure SDLC artifacts request — Acme FS assessment

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this assessment. As part of our SOC 2 / SIG intake for Acme Financial Services we need a compact evidence package covering your Secure SDLC controls. Specifically we're looking for:

- Current code review policy (who approves, required checks)
- CI/CD gating config showing blocked merges on failing checks
- Secrets scanning & rotation evidence (tool outputs + rotation logs)
- Change approval/audit trail for production deploys (Q1)
- Supply-chain artifacts (SBOM snapshot, dependency-scan results)
- Credential-detector run results and metrics (false positive rate, detection coverage)

If possible please bundle artifacts in a single secure Drive link and flag any PHI/keys for redaction. Target deadline: 2027-04-22 EOD.

Thanks,
Todd Ramirez
Acme Security (third-party assessor)

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: audit@acme-sec.com, todd.ramirez@acmeinc.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC artifacts request — Acme FS assessment

Todd — thanks for the checklist. We're on it.

Plan / owners:
- Code review policy & sample PR workflow: Marissa (attached policy + sample PR link)
- CI gating config + pipeline runs: Dev (CI exports + run IDs)
- Secrets rotation audit & KMS rotation proof: Neha (rotation logs)
- SBOM + dependency scan: I will include the SBOM snapshot and the dependency scan CSV.
- Credential-detector report: Dev will include the latest run and a short note on FP rate/tuning.

We will sanitize any secrets/KMS ARNs before sharing. If you need signed attestations for particular artifacts, please call that out. We'll upload a single Drive folder and post the link once ready — aim to have it to you by 2027-04-20 to give you time to review ahead of your 22nd deadline.

-Markus
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.example.com
To: audit@acme-sec.com, todd.ramirez@acmeinc.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-04-20T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC artifacts request — uploads and brief notes

Todd / team — uploading the artifacts now. Summary of what's in the Drive folder (Drive link later in this thread):

1) code-review-policy-v2.pdf — our policy requiring two approvers for service-level PRs, one approver for docs/config, and the "no direct pushes to main" rule. Includes required LGTM labels and protected-branch gating.

2) ci-gate-config-20270415.yaml — the GitHub Actions pipeline that gates merges. Key checks: unit-test, integration-smoke, license-scan, dependency-scan, credential-detector. The workflow contains required status checks against the branch protection rules.

3) credential-detector-report-20270416.csv — output of our custom credential detector (pattern + entropy heuristics) for the last 14 days. Columns: file_path, match_type, confidence, action_taken. 
   - FP note: We observed ~7% false positive rate on test corpus (internal eval) after tuning; we mark low-confidence matches for manual triage.

4) supplychain-sbom-20270416.json — SBOM snapshot for the service components in scope (CycloneDX format).

5) secrets-rotation-audit-20270416.csv — KMS rotation events (redacted key ids) for Jan–Apr 2027; shows automated monthly rotation. Full rotation logs are stored in our internal KMS audit system — we can export signed logs if required.

6) change-approval-log-2027Q1.csv — exports from the change-approval system showing approvals, approvers, and granted deploy windows for production deploys in Q1.

Attachments referenced above are in the Drive folder. All credentials/ARNs are redacted; we have included run IDs for CI builds where you can request artifacts.

From: Acme Security <audit@acme-sec.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-04-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC artifacts request — follow-ups

Dev / Markus — thanks for the prompt upload. A couple of clarifying items before we close the ticket: 

- Credential detector: can you provide the evaluation script + seed corpus so we can validate the 7% FP figure? Also please confirm how high-entropy false positives are handled in the pipeline (auto-block vs. manual triage).
- Secrets rotation: the CSV is helpful but we need a signed export (HMAC) from your KMS audit system for rotation events for two sample keys (we can redact ARNs after receiving).
- CI runs: please provide two example CI run IDs and links so we can fetch the raw logs for the gating checks.

One more ask: can you confirm whether third-party CI actions (marketplace actions) are pinned to specific SHAs or whether you rely on version tags only?

If possible send these by EOD 2027-04-22 or let us know if you need a short call.

Thanks,
Todd
Acme Security

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: audit@acme-sec.com, todd.ramirez@acmeinc.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-04-22T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC artifacts request — final uploads & notes

Todd — we uploaded the additional items and answered your clarifying questions. Highlights below and links in the Drive folder: 

- Credential detector eval artifacts: evaluation script (eval_credential_detector.py), seed corpus (redacted test set), and the detailed false-positive analysis. Our pipeline marks high-confidence matches as "auto-flag" which blocks the merge; medium/low confidence are routed to the security-triage queue (manual).

- KMS rotation proof: signed export (HMAC-signed) for two sample keys has been added (secrets-rotation-signed-20270422.json). ARNs were redacted; if you need the full ARNs we can provide them under an NDA addendum — otherwise the HMAC proves integrity.

- CI run artifacts: two CI builds with run IDs 20270415-jenkins-12345 and gh-20270414-6789 (links in the Drive folder). Those contain raw logs for the gating checks and the dependency scan artifacts.

- Third-party actions: we pin marketplace actions to SHAs for all actions used in production pipelines; we keep an internal mapping file (actions-pinlist.csv) which is included.

Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/secure/Acme-SDLC-Pack-20270418
HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.example.com/ticket/ACME-4921 (status: evidence-provided)

If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough of any of the artifacts, Marissa and I can join — propose a few slots and we'll confirm.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference
